solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Records part of search I've started

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the run of letters in the following words, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run on across these words, from the end of search into started

explanation.surface: Someone checking old documents finds they form part of a search already begun.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical documents, so they are stored records.

clue.text: A female relation displaying a good nature

parts.note: taken as written
a relation can be a story or account, as is a fable

explanation.surface: A kindly woman in the family who is good-natured.
explanation.walkthrough: Relation looks like a family member but means a recounted story.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means friendly and easy to talk to, i.e. good-natured.

clue.text: Excellent form!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal adjective for top quality
second meaning: a school year group

explanation.definitionFit: Class means stylish quality and is also a group of pupils taught together, a school form.

clue.text: One prince lying in state, not breathing out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the prince's name rests inside the word for state

parts.note: a nation is a state or country
Hal is Prince Henry in Shakespeare's Henry IV

explanation.surface: A royal lying in state is, grimly, no longer breathing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lying in state suggests a dead royal, but it is the instruction to put the name inside a word for country.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhalation is drawing breath in, the reverse of exhaling.

clue.text: Means to escape, say, on steam ship

parts.note: eg means for example, as does say
re means about or on, concerning

explanation.surface: A way to flee, for instance aboard a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit, a way out of a place.

clue.text: Relative to visit frequently in E London?

indicators.note: said the Cockney way of the East End, which drops the initial H

parts.note: to haunt a place is to visit it often

explanation.surface: A question about whether a relative is someone to go and see often in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney, the dialect of the East End of London, famously drops its aitches, so a Cockney's word for frequenting a place loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family relation.

clue.text: Scotland's representative in on RUC reforms

indicators.note: reforms means shapes again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish delegate has a hand in police reorganisation in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police force until 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is Scotland's national animal and appears on the royal coat of arms for Scotland.

clue.text: Giant bird on land, wingless

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: with its wings, i.e. the outer letters at each side, cut off

parts.note: taken with its end letters removed

explanation.surface: A huge bird lands but cannot fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giant deities of Greek myth, so a titan is a colossus.

clue.text: Dread about the unknown, such as birds?

indicators.note: the word for dread goes around, or about, the next word

parts.note: fear is a synonym of dread
taken as written
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A fear of the unknown, likened to how birds might feel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: birds are covered in feathers, so they could be called feathery.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds have plumage made of feathers, so feathery describes things like them.

clue.text: Fortune initially told after thirty seconds?

indicators.note: the letter from told is placed after the half-minute piece

parts.note: half a minute, so half the letters of the word minute

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller's reading delivered after just thirty seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirty seconds is half a minute, and the first half of the word MINUTE is MIN, also its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a mint is to earn a huge amount of money, a fortune.

clue.text: Relative violently anti-Greece

indicators.note: violent change throws the letters into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member fiercely opposed to Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-niece is the granddaughter of one's brother or sister, a kinswoman.

clue.text: Fellow arts graduates I left

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, so two or more are BAs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man notes that the arts graduates have gone and he alone has left.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a man's name, and a fellow is a man.

clue.text: Knight, behold, has popular beef

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A knight is told to look: he has some well-liked beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirloin is a prime cut of beef from the loin.

clue.text: No longer is? That's spurious, firstly!

definitions.text: No longer is? That's spurious, firstly!

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what it was
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letters of the words before it are taken

parts.note: the first letters of these two words supply the ending

explanation.surface: Someone rejects the claim that something has ceased to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: saying a thing no longer is would be false, because it still is.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be present or real, which is the opposite of having ceased to be.

clue.text: Forbidden to enter vaudeville gallery

indicators.note: the answer lies within the following words, entering them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of vaudeville and the start of gallery

explanation.surface: Access to the balcony at a music hall is off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Vaudeville is variety theatre; its gallery is the top tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal means prohibited by law, so not permitted.

clue.text: Publication by Web is something attractive

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical publication
the Net and the Web are both names for the internet

explanation.surface: An online magazine is said to be appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet draws iron to it, and figuratively draws people, so it attracts.

clue.text: Like patterned cloth, all square, you had once

parts.note: level scores, so the match is tied
ye is an old form of you, so ye'd is an old way of saying you had

explanation.surface: A description of chequered fabric once owned by you.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-dyed fabric is knotted before dyeing to create swirled patterns.

clue.text: Home closed twice, completely

indicators.note: twice means the word for closed is used a second time

parts.note: in means at home
to, as in pushing a door to, means closed

explanation.surface: Someone's house is shut up twice over, entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: IN then TO and TO again. A door pushed to is closed.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for in total, meaning entirely or as a whole.

clue.text: Everyone taken in by benefit that's subject to inflation

indicators.note: one word is held inside the other, as if taken in by it

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
all means everyone

explanation.surface: An economic remark about a welfare payment that will rise with the cost of living.
explanation.walkthrough: Inflation suggests prices and welfare payments, but here it is blowing air into something.
explanation.definitionFit: A balloon is filled with air or gas, so it is a thing that gets blown up.

clue.text: Like to be in bed, it's established

indicators.note: the word for like goes inside the word bed

parts.note: taken as written
as means like, in the same way

explanation.surface: Someone who enjoys a lie-in finds it a settled fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Based means founded or grounded on something, i.e. set up.

clue.text: Count, perhaps, on returning book and French article

indicators.note: going back, so the word on is read right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A count heading back to a French book.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a rank of nobleman, an example of an aristocrat; perhaps signals the example.

clue.text: Orwell's British resting place

definitions.note: read as Orwell is, the apostrophe-s being the link

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den where it rests

explanation.surface: Where the British writer Orwell was laid to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: Blair was the real surname of the author known as George Orwell.

clue.text: Wise thing to put in stuffing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as an adjective, wise and learned
second meaning: the herb used in ... and onion stuffing

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for wisdom and a herb, classically paired with onion in stuffing for poultry.

clue.text: Girl who's wayward so may err

indicators.note: letters that go astray are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl with an unruly streak is liable to go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Daughter, unwell, getting one in a pickle?

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A daughter falls ill and finds herself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: In a pickle sounds like being in difficulty, but it is literal: the herb flavours pickled cucumbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is the herb used to flavour pickled gherkins, known as dill pickles.

clue.text: Shabby party clothes found by journalist

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
gear is informal for clothing
ed is short for editor, a newspaper journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter discovers some scruffy outfits from a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-eared pages have worn, turned-down corners, so it means worn and tatty.
